full_judgment:
B. K. Das J:- This petition for leave to appeal has been filed against the judgment and order dated 28.4.2008 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Order No. 1775 of 2008 summarily rejecting an application filed under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure affirming the judgment and decree dated 17.10.2007 passed by the Second Court of the Joint District Judge, Mymensingh in Other Class Appeal No. 82 of 2008 who upheld the judgment and decree dated 31.1.2006 passed by the Senior Assistant, Sadar Mymensingh in Title Suit No. 55 of 2005 dismissing the plaintiff's' suit. 

 4. The defendant Nos. 1-5 contested the suit by filing a written statement contending that admittedly Gagon Chandra Saha and his brother Nagor Bashi Shaha got the suit land by a decree of a partition suit and the suit land fell in the saham of Gagon Chandra Saha and Gagon Chandra Saha while in possession of the suit land made a gift in favour of his daughter Minoti Bala Saha by executing a registered deed of gift No. 2953 dated 26.3.1963 and put the done in possession of the suit land and that while in such possession Minoti Bala Saha transferred the suit land in favour of defendant Nos. 1-5 by the kabala No. 146 dated 4.1.2000 and put the defendant Nos. 1-5 in possession of the suit land. The contesting defendants further claimed that they are in possession of the suit land and that the plaintiffs have no title or possession therein and prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 5. The trial court on consideration of the evidence on record found that the suit land fell in the saham of Gagon Chandra Saha vide judgment and decree passed in Partition Suit No. 37 of 1959 and that Gagon Chandra Saha while in possession of the suit land made a gift of the suit land in favour of his daughter Minoti Bala Saha by registered deed of gift No. 2953 dated 26.3.1963 and put her in possession. The trial court further found that Minoti Bala Saha while in possession of the suit land transferred the 'suit land in favour of defendant Nos. 1-5 by a registered sale deed No. 146 dated 4.1.2000. The trial court further found that the plaintiffs could not produce any evidence to prove that the registered deed of gift is a forged one. The trial court further found that the plaintiffs could not produce any evidence to prove that they are owners of the suit land by inheritance and that the deed of gift executed by Gagon Chandra and the sale deed executed by Minoti Bala Saha were forged and fabricated. The trial court accordingly found that the plaintiffs have no title to the suit land and the suit as filed was not maintainable and accordingly dis-missed the suit. 

 6. Against the said judgment and decree the plaintiff preferred Other Appeal No.82 of 2006 before the learned District Judge, Mymensingh. The learned Joint District Judge, Second Court, Mymensingh who heard the said appeal concurred with the decision of the trial court on all the issues and thereby found that the plaintiffs failed to prove that the deed of gift executed by Gagon Chandra Saha in favour of his daughter Minoti Bala Saha is a forged and fabricated document. The appellate court considered the evidence on record and accepted the finding of the trial court that the plaintiff failed to prove that the sale deed dated 4.1.2000 executed by Minoti Bala Saha in favour of defendant Nos. 1-5 is forged and fabricated. The lower appellate court on consideration of the evidence on record held that the plaintiffs failed to establish their title to the suit land by inheritance and accordingly the suit as framed was not maintainable. The lower appellate court by judgment and decree dated 17.10.2007 dismissed the appeal and affirmed the decision of the trial court. 

 9. The learned counsel appearing for the plaintiffs Petitioners submits that the High Court Division committed an error of law in failing to notice that the deed of gift dated 26.3.1963 was not a valid document and thus Minoti Bala Saha did not acquire any title on the basis of the said deed of gift. The trial court found that in a decree passed in partition suit no. 37, of 1959 the suit land fell in the saham of Gagan Saha and thus the registered deed of gift executed by Gagan Saha in favour of his daughter Minoti Bala was a valid document and the lower appellate court on consideration of the evidence concurred with the said finding of the trial court and thus the finding of the High Court Division that "The Appellate court below also observed that the gift deed in favour of Minoti is valid and that after 41 years of the registration of the deed and thereby the plaintiff failed to prove his case." does not suffer from any illegality. The learned Counsel further submits that the defendant Nos. 1-5 did not acquire any title on the basis of the kabala dated 4.1.2000 and that the High Court Division misread and misconstrued the evidence and failed to notice that .the plaintiffs acquired title to the suit land on the basis of inheritance. The learned Advocate also submits that the High Court Division` committed an error of law in failing to notice that the courts below without assessing the evidence on record and with-out considering the genuineness of the deed of gift summarily rejected the revisional application which is not tenable in law.
